_source_corrections: Media/screen-recordings/LIBRARY.md describes this recording as '1080x1920, 10.3s'. Both numbers are wrong and I only found it by looking: ffprobe reports 26.36s at 25fps, and the app content is a 540x960 capture padded into the 1080x1920 canvas with flat grey 128 (measured by scanning a decoded frame for the non-pad bounding box -- content occupies rows 0..959, cols 0..539 exactly). So every shot takes src_crop 540:960:0:0 and is upscaled 2x, which is clean because 540x960 is already 9:16. Without that crop the app sits in one corner and three quarters of the frame is grey -- which is exactly what the first build of this video shipped.
_shot_rhythm: Only ONE indexed portrait Dossie recording exists, so variety comes from WHERE in it each cut lands. The take is a real journey and roughly the first 9s is the sign-in screen (including a masked password field) -- useless for a capability demo and faintly bad-looking, so nothing before t=10 is used. The TREC deadlines payoff lives at t=19-26 and carries the three PROOF cuts. No synthetic push anywhere: the footage is already upscaled 2x and a zoom on top would only soften it further. This is still the weakest of the three on visual variety, and the honest fix is more app footage, not more effects -- see README.
